paragraphs.text: Solar panels need space, and in crowded countries land is expensive. One solution is to place panels on water. Floating solar farms have been built on reservoirs, lakes and even flooded quarries.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Water has an unexpected advantage: it keeps the panels cool. Solar panels work less efficiently when they are hot, and tests in Singapore found that floating panels produced up to 10 per cent more electricity than similar panels on nearby rooftops.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The panels also shade the water, which reduces evaporation. This is particularly useful for reservoirs that supply drinking water in dry regions.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Engineers are still studying the effects on wildlife. Covering too much of a lake could reduce the light reaching underwater plants, so most projects cover no more than a third of the surface.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Several countries in Asia and Europe are now planning much larger floating farms, some covering areas the size of hundreds of football pitches.
paragraphs.label: E

items.quote: Floating solar farms have been built on reservoirs, lakes and even flooded quarries
items.prompt: Apart from reservoirs and lakes, where have floating solar farms been built?

explanation.en: “built on reservoirs, lakes and even flooded quarries” → flooded quarries. Reservoirs and lakes are excluded by “Apart from”.
explanation.kk: «built on reservoirs, lakes and even flooded quarries» → flooded quarries. Су қоймасы мен көлді сұрақтың өзі («Apart from») алып тастайды.
explanation.ru: «built on reservoirs, lakes and even flooded quarries» → flooded quarries. Водохранилища и озёра исключены самим вопросом («Apart from»).

items.quote: tests in Singapore found that floating panels produced up to 10 per cent more electricity
items.prompt: In which country were the floating panels tested?

explanation.en: The tests took place in Singapore: “tests in Singapore found that floating panels produced …”. The country comes just before the result → Singapore.
explanation.kk: Сынақ Сингапурда өткен: «tests in Singapore found that floating panels produced …». Ел атауы тәжірибе нәтижесінің алдында тұр → Singapore.
explanation.ru: Испытания проводили в Сингапуре: «tests in Singapore found that floating panels produced …». Страна стоит прямо перед результатом опыта → Singapore.

items.quote: produced up to 10 per cent more electricity than similar panels on nearby rooftops
items.prompt: By how much more electricity did the floating panels produce?

explanation.en: “produced up to 10 per cent more electricity” → 10 per cent (or 10%). You can leave out “up to”, which would push you over the limit.
explanation.kk: «produced up to 10 per cent more electricity» → 10 per cent (немесе 10%). «Up to» жазбауға болады — шек онсыз да толуға жақын.
explanation.ru: «produced up to 10 per cent more electricity» → 10 per cent (или 10%). «Up to» можно не писать — лимит и так почти исчерпан.

items.quote: The panels also shade the water, which reduces evaporation
items.prompt: What does the shade from the panels reduce?

explanation.en: “shade the water, which reduces evaporation” → evaporation. Drinking water in the next sentence is the benefit, not what is reduced.
explanation.kk: «shade the water, which reduces evaporation» → evaporation. Келесі сөйлемдегі ауыз су — азаятын нәрсе емес, пайда.
explanation.ru: «shade the water, which reduces evaporation» → evaporation. Питьевая вода в следующем предложении — польза, а не то, что уменьшается.

items.quote: most projects cover no more than a third of the surface
items.prompt: What is the largest part of a lake’s surface that most projects cover?

explanation.en: “cover no more than a third of the surface” → a third. “Largest part” paraphrases “no more than”.
explanation.kk: «cover no more than a third of the surface» → a third. «Largest part» — «no more than» дегеннің басқаша айтылымы.
explanation.ru: «cover no more than a third of the surface» → a third. «Largest part» пересказывает «no more than».
